test_title: PYST 3: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 07 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: In post 1991 reforms, the term 'disinvestment' refers to:

options.text: selling government's share in public sector companies

solution:
The correct answer is __**selling government's share in public sector companies**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **disinvestment** refers to the process of the government selling its stake in **public sector undertakings (PSUs)** to private entities or the public. This is done to reduce the financial burden on the government and to improve efficiency in these enterprises.
 
• **Disinvestment in India** gained momentum during the **1991 economic reforms** when India liberalized its economy to address the balance of payments crisis and introduced structural reforms.
 
• Disinvestment is aimed at raising resources for the government and promoting private-sector participation in industries to improve **competition, operational efficiency, and profitability.**
 
• Under disinvestment, the government may sell a part or whole of its equity in PSUs to private entities or individuals through mechanisms like **public offers, strategic sales, or auctions.**
 
• The proceeds from disinvestment are used for purposes like reducing the fiscal deficit, infrastructure development, and funding social welfare programs. *Hence, the correct answer is selling government's share in public sector companies.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of Disinvestment:**

 
 
• To reduce the **financial burden** of the government and generate revenue for developmental projects.
 
• To improve the **efficiency and competitiveness** of public sector enterprises.
 
• To promote wider participation by the private sector and the public, ensuring greater accountability and transparency.
 
 
 
• **Methods of Disinvestment:**
 
 
• The government can undertake **strategic sales**, where it sells a significant portion of its shareholding in PSUs to private entities.
 
• Public offers involve the sale of shares in PSUs to the general public through the **stock market.**
 
 
 
• **Examples of Disinvestment in India:**
 
 
• **1999: Modern Foods** was sold to Hindustan Unilever, marking one of the first major strategic sales.
 
• **2000s:** Companies like **VSNL, Balco, and Hindustan Zinc** were divested to private entities.
 
• **Recent examples:** The government has divested its stake in companies like **Air India (2021) and LIC (2022).**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Legal Framework:**

 
 
• Disinvestment policies are governed by the **Department of Investment and Public Asset Management (DIPAM),** which oversees the disinvestment process.
 
• The government also sets annual targets for disinvestment in its **Union Budget.**
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Disinvestment:**
 
 
• Resistance from **labor unions** and employees of PSUs due to job security concerns.
 
• Opposition from political entities who view disinvestment as a loss of national assets.
 
• Difficulty in finding suitable buyers for loss-making enterprises.
